pressure.title: Lifting sewage to a higher sewer
pressure.description: Gravity sewers get deeper downstream; a lift station raises the flow into a rising (force) main or a higher sewer. Pumps start and stop on level so they do not cycle too often (typically ≤ 6–10 starts/h per motor — wet-well volume is sized for it) and the duty alternates. Non-clog impellers pass solids (often ≥ 75–100 mm); rising-main velocity is kept ≈ 0.7–2.5 m/s to avoid settling. Pumps lift out on the guide rails without anyone entering the well — a confined space with H₂S risk.

foundation: Reinforced-concrete tank on prepared ground; watertightness test before backfill; allow for buoyancy when empty (groundwater).
alignment: Weirs and launders levelled to a few millimetres so overflow is even; drive/bridge centred and level.
piping: Inlet arranged to spread flow without short-circuiting; sludge lines with flushing points; overflow and drain to a safe place.
commissioning: Fill with clean water, check for leaks; run mechanisms empty and with water; start chemical dosing and tune by jar tests.

routine.task: Check run hours, alarms and basket.

periodic.task: Clean floats; check pump insulation and seal monitor.

lubrication: Motor and drive bearings greased / oiled to maker schedule; gearbox oil changed by hours or oil analysis.

safety: Confined space permits, gas testing; lock-out; vent odour.

video_tutorials.title: Sewage Lift Station — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Sewage Lift Station.
A sewage lift station collects sewage in a wet well and pumps it up into a rising main or higher sewer.
Submersible non-clog pumps sit on duckfoot bends and can be lifted out on guide rails; floats or a level transmitter start and stop them; check and gate valves sit in a separate dry valve chamber.
Typical applications include municipal and plant sewage networks; industrial site drainage and effluent transfer.

video_tutorials.title: Sewage Lift Station — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Sewage Lift Station.
Check run hours, alarms and basket.
Clean floats; check pump insulation and seal monitor.
Lift pumps; replace seals/wear parts.
Watch for pump ragging: high current, low flow. Common cause: wipes and rags.
Watch for high-level alarm: flooding risk. Common cause: pump failure, power cut.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
